If the discriminant is positive, two real roots exist. Use the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a). Plug the values in, and simplify to find the roots. This method works for all real coefficients.

To find stationary points of y=f(x), first take the first derivative, f'(x). Set f'(x) equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Plug them back into the original function to find the corresponding y-values.
